title: Green Finance Week Asia 2026 Concludes in Singapore, Mobilizing Institutional Capital for Asia's Net-Zero Transition
detail: Green Finance Week: Asia 2026 concluded May 13 at Singapore's Four Points by Sheraton Riverview, convening 100+ decision-makers and 25+ speakers from institutional investors, sovereign wealth funds, development banks, and governments to accelerate Asia's clean energy transition. Key sessions addressed barriers to institutional climate finance in emerging Asian markets, regional grid interconnection for renewable energy, and ESG investment frameworks. Verdant Energy was recognized as Clean Energy Investor of the Year. Knowledge partners included the Singapore Green Finance Centre (SGFC) and Asia Investor Group on Climate Change (AIGCC). Singapore's role as Asia's green finance hub has grown significantly: Singapore-based green bond issuance rose 38% in 2025, and the Monetary Authority of Singapore has committed $2 billion to catalyze private green finance across Southeast Asia. The event comes as Asia-Pacific now accounts for over half of global clean energy investment, led by China, India, Japan, and South Korea.

media.caption: Green Finance Week Asia 2026 concludes in Singapore — 100+ institutional investors align on Asia clean energy capital deployment

title: Philippines' AboitizPower Confirms ₱62 Billion ($1.06B) Renewable Energy and BESS Capex for 2026, 639 MW Pipeline
detail: AboitizPower, the Philippines' largest power generator with a 23.86% share of the national generation market, confirmed ₱62 billion (~$1.06 billion USD) in capital expenditure for 2026, with the majority directed at new renewable energy projects and battery energy storage systems (BESS). The company holds a 639.5 MW renewable project pipeline awarded through the 4th Green Energy Auction Program (GEAP) in September 2025, with 147 MW already under active construction. AboitizPower has scaled its attributable net sellable renewable capacity from under 1 GW in 2020 to 2.3 GW by early 2026. The Philippines targets 35% of electricity generation from renewables by 2030 and 50% by 2040, and the country's competitive renewable energy auctions are driving rapid capacity growth. The company's investment also reflects the broader Southeast Asian clean energy acceleration: the region added a record 27 GW of solar in 2025, up 45% year-on-year.

media.caption: AboitizPower confirms ₱62B renewable capex with 639 MW pipeline — Philippines' green energy buildout accelerates
